title: Oil price surge expected to flip Alberta's projected $9.4B deficit into $8.5B surplus
summary: Alberta's government says the oil-rich province is on track to reach record-high resource revenues this year.

image.caption: Finance Minister Jason Nixon, shown here speaking to media at the Alberta legislature on Dec. 10, 2025, provided the provincial government's second-quarter fiscal update Thursday. (Amber Bracken/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Alberta's government says the oil-rich province is on track to reach record-high resource revenues this year.
Minister says province focused on fiscal discipline, economic strength and strategic investments
· Posted: Nov 26, 2026 2:19 PM EST | Last Updated: 31 minutes ago
Its second fiscal update of the year predicts a $8.5-billion surplus — a wild swing from the $9.4-billion deficit originally expected for the 2026-27 fiscal year.
Alberta's finances are tethered to global energy prices, which surged earlier this year after the U.S.-Iran conflict began.
In February, the province was predicting West Texas Intermediate — the North American benchmark oil price — would average US$60.50 a barrel this year.
Alberta is now forecasting that price to be US$83.50 per barrel, driven by disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping lane at the mouth of the Persian Gulf.

blocks.text: In the 2022 fiscal year, the province took in a record $25-billion in resource revenues, but the province expects to break that with almost $29 billion this year.
Finance Minister Jason Nixon says the government remains focused on fiscal discipline, economic strength and strategic investments.
Lisa Johnson is a reporter for The Canadian Press based in Alberta.
